projects.name: UNESCO: Cultural Heritage Resilience in North Macedonia
projects.description:
UNESCO and UNDP are jointly developing CHERISH – Cultural Heritage Resilience in South-East Europe, a regional climate-resilience initiative spanning the Western Balkans and including North Macedonia. The programme responds to rising climate impacts – droughts, floods, heatwaves, wildfires, and land degradation – that are eroding cultural landscapes, traditional water systems, and heritage-based rural economies. CHERISH positions cultural and natural heritage as a climate-relevant asset and aligns with national adaptation priorities, NDCs, and EU Green Deal processes.

As the project is still in development, the initial phase will focus on establishing key baselines, mapping priority heritage systems, and preparing a full climate-finance proposal. The long-term vision is to restore and climate-proof heritage systems, support community-led adaptation mechanisms, strengthen climate-resilient tourism and green enterprises, and integrate heritage-based adaptation into national and local planning. This joint effort offers a scalable regional model for resilience and sustainable development.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1: Climate Action and Resilience to Disaster and Humanitarian Risks

projects.name: UNDP: EU For Prespa - Infrastructure Improvements in the Prespa Area
projects.description:
The Project “EU for Infrastructure Improvements in the Prespa Area” is an important part of the broader “EU for Prespa” Action, aiming at promoting the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans in the transboundary Prespa Lake area in line with the principle of "leaving no persons and regions behind."
The Project comprises a set of interrelated capital investments for infrastructure development and accompanying measures with far reaching beneficial impacts for the entire transboundary Prespa Lake basin/Prespa Park area.
The Project will contribute to the preservation and improvement of the ecological system in the Prespa Lake area through a series of interlinked capital investments to be implemented within the boundaries of the Municipality of Resen and accompanying capacity development measures. These initiatives are designed to enhance municipal wastewater and solid waste management systems, redirecting harmful pollutants away from natural ecosystems. The Municipality of Resen and the public utility “Proleter” will benefit from carefully planned capacity development efforts, ensuring the sustainability of the newly introduced systems, and resulting communal wastewater and solid waste management services.
Furthermore, the Project will contribute to enhancing transboundary cooperation and improving connectivity and mobility around the lake, through the opening of a new border crossing point with Greece, at Markova Noga. This, in turn, is expected to boost socio-economic and tourism development while fostering cooperation among the nations sharing the lake basin. All of this aligns with the main provisions of the International Agreement for the Protection and Sustainable Development of Prespa Park and the trilateral Strategic Action Plan for Prespa Park. 
The partners and beneficiaries of the Project are the Customs Administration (for the border crossing), the Municipality of Resen, the public utility "Proleter" as well as communities, households, and businesses benefiting from the newly introduced systems. The Project shall be implemented in close collaboration with the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning and multiple other stakeholders at national and local levels.

projects.name: UNDP: Green Finance Facility to Improve Air Quality & Combat Climate Change in North Macedonia
projects.description: The Green Finance Facility (GFF) is an innovative financial mechanism that enables affordable finance to small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) and marketable but underserved households to adopt renewable energy (RE) and efficient energy (EE) technology solutions. The facility provides loans for RE and/or EE through partner financial institutions, supported by technical assistance and ex-post performance-based payments for completed and verified RE and/or EE projects. GFF enabled adoption of RE and EE solutions will contribute to reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution and will strengthen the local ecosystem for RE & EE green finance. Outcome 2: Target groups, especially women and female headed households have greater access to finance for accelerating a transition to renewable energy and energy efficiency solutions. For households, the facility will provide US$ 6.5 million in loans through local banks, with an expected IRR of 5 - 6%. This will be complemented by performance- based payments equal to up to 30% of the original loan amount. Outcome 2 specifically targets female-headed households, single-parents, households with PWD, Roma households, and employees who were affected by COVID-19. To tap into remittances, the project also targets remittance recipients and returning migrants.

The support focuses on improving strategic planning, coordination, and implementation of EU-related reforms, enhancing alignment with the EU acquis, and reinforcing institutional capacities across priority negotiation areas. Through targeted technical assistance, capacity building, and inclusive dialogue, the initiative promotes good governance, rule of law, fundamental rights, media and youth engagement, contributing to a more effective, transparent, and sustainable European integration process.

projects.name: UNDP: Scaling-up actions to tackle air pollution

The project will be built on the results achieved and lessons learnt from the first project phase and will aim at scaling up and replication of the concept, that was developed and applied, in five other cities in the country that have serious issues with the air pollution: Kavadarci, Gostivar, Kumanovo, Strumica and Struga.

projects.name: UNDP: EU for Prespa - Restoration of natural resources and enhancing sustainable agriculture and tourism
projects.description:
The objective of the overall Action “EU for Prespa” is to promote the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans in the transboundary Prespa Lake area in line with the “no persons and regions left behind”. 
The Specific Objective of the Project “Restoration of natural resources and enhancing sustainable agriculture and tourism” is to instigate a significant change in practices and behaviour among policy makers at local level, farmers, private sector, CSO and citizens regarding the management of and the sustainable use of natural resources in the Prespa region which will result in improved quality of life and contribute to economic development by emerging “green” pathways to growth.
The EU investments will contribute to the preservation of the natural capital and restore the damaged ecosystem of Macro Prespa Lake to good ecological status, in line with EU standards. The measures will address the pollution of water and soil, protect endangered species and encourage the sustainability of the local economic and agricultural practices. The farmers, households, and small businesses will be supported to apply good agricultural practices, create small chain value, and invest in sustainable tourism services and products respectively. The Project shall also enhance the cross-border cooperation by supporting the creation of a new vision for sustainable development of the Prespa Lakes region. 

This overall goal of the Project will be achieved through three outcomes: 
Outcome 1: The ecological system in Prespa Lake area preserved and improved
Outcome 2: Sustainable economic activities in Prespa area boosted
Outcome 3: Enhanced cross-border cooperation

The main Project partners and beneficiaries are the Municipality of Resen, farmers and farmer associations, households and entities engaged in sustainable tourism from the Prespa region.
The Project shall be implemented in close collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy, the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning and the Prespa Park Management Committee.

projects.name: UNDP: Climate Promise II – Revision of the National Determine Contributions - NDC 3.0
projects.description:
The project "Climate Promise II – Revision of the National Determine Contributions – NDC 3.0" focuses on revising the National Determined Contributions in North Macedonia as a comprehensive national strategy aimed at accelerating climate action and sustainable development. The project aims to raise the country’s ambition for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, in line with the Paris Agreement and European Union climate policies. This means setting stronger targets for emission reductions and integrating climate action into the country’s broader economic, social, and environmental development plans. 

A key aspect of NDC 3.0 is its inclusive approach where the process involves active participation from government institutions, civil society, youth, women, and vulnerable groups, ensuring that climate action is fair, transparent, and leaves no one behind. The project also emphasizes sustainable management of natural resources, where efforts are directed at pollution control, biodiversity protection, sustainable agriculture, and improved waste management. 

Institutional strengthening is another major focus of the project, with measures to improve coordination among ministries, build capacity at the local level, and ensure effective governance of climate policies. The main goal is to establish transparent systems for monitoring, reporting, and verifying progress.

projects.name: ILO: National OSH framework conducive to the promotion of a safe and healthy working environment is in place
projects.description:
The ILO will support the development of a sound, gender-sensitive national legal- and policy framework as the critical starting point for ensuring a safe and healthy working environment. To this end, the ILO will support stakeholders to effectively engage in the legislative and policy processes needed to bring the legal and policy frameworks in line with International Labour Standards and the related EU acquis. A comprehensive gap analysis of the harmonisation of the national OSH legislation (laws and bylaws) with ratified ILO conventions and the EU OSH Directives will be conducted. The ILO Support Kit for Developing Occupational Safety and Health Legislation will be used to prepare all necessary changes to align the legislation. The ILO will also assess the current system of employment injury compensation and insurance and develop recommendations for possible system redesign. 
A gender sensitive national OSH Profile will be developed/updated as an important step towards building a solid OSH policy and a new National Strategy on OSH which addresses the different risks and health needs of women and men. National OSH Policy and Strategy will be developed in line with the EU Strategic Framework on Health and Safety at work 2021-2027. The OSH Profile is an instrument which entails a systematic review and evaluation of the national situation with respect to occupational accidents and diseases as well as of the entire range of instruments and resources available in the country to implement the OSH Policy. It will identify strong points, weak points and gaps in North Macedonia’s OSH system and will be used to identify priority issues for the national OSH Policy.

projects.name: ILO: Systems and procedures for improved labour inspection services are in place
projects.description:
With the ILO support, the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI) will be transformed and modernized. The SLI plays a crucial role in securing a safe and healthy working environment in North Macedonia. The ILO will support the revision/development and digitalisation of all inspection processes, reporting procedures, analytical functions, and planning. To this end, the SLI information management system will be upgraded. The ILO will support development of methodology and software for risk assessment in planning the inspection visits. ILO will support development a training curriculum for labour inspectors, based on the preceding LI training needs assessment. In cooperation with the Government, a SLI training and education centre will be established and equipped. Furthermore, we will upgrade the ILO-supported SLI learning platform for the labour inspectors in North Macedonia, by developing new learning modules and specific trainings (for instance, on OSH data analysis). SLI will, moreover, be granted the access to all ILO tools and methodologies that will support its transformation in a modern and efficient labour inspectorate.
The ILO will support the participation of national stakeholders in various EU-OSHA and ILO surveys. Targeted training for the staff of the Ministry of Economy and Labour and the State Labour Inspectorate will ensure that these institutions have the critical staff to respond to the obligations in the area of OSH, stemming from the EU negotiations process and later from the EU membership.

projects.name: ILO: Improved OSH Information system and procedures are in place
projects.description:
A key enabler for the progressive improvement and resilience of occupational safety and health frameworks is the development of evidence-based research, coupled with a mechanism for the collection and analysis of occupational safety and health data. In addition to developing national recording and notification systems on occupational injuries and diseases, the ILO will support robust research on occupational safety and health, thereby fostering a proactive approach to the prevention of hazards and mitigation of risks.
ILO will support building of the evidence base effectively feeding the processes of design, monitoring and evaluation of legislation, policies and interventions. Comprehensive and accurate data will strengthen the occupational safety and health system at national level and within enterprises and will facilitate effective allocation of scarce public resources. Following an assessment of the current situation, the ILO will implement combined actions at national and workplace level to improve the data collection, reporting and notification on work-related accidents, occupational injuries, and occupation diseases, in line with the European Statistics on Accidents at Work and European Occupational Diseases Statistics methodologies. The ILO will support preparation of the necessary legal framework for the information system and will develop the web-based OSH information system for collecting, recording, processing, and reporting on occupational accidents and diseases. The online OSH information system platform is aimed at revolutionizing workplace safety management in North Macedonia. By providing real-time data on the number of workers, companies, workplace accidents, specific risks, industry-wide hazards, health trends, and related costs, this platform will empower North Macedonia to continuously monitor and improve its occupational safety landscape. The insights gained will support the development of effective safety and health strategies, targeted action plans, and timely preventive measures, ultimately benefiting all citizens and enhancing workplace safety standards nationwide.

ILO will provide manuals on labour inspection, OSH rulebooks, and will provide trainings on OSH for employers and workers. projects.name: FAO: Support country decarbonization process through integrated management of forest fires and strengthening climate information sharing
projects.description:
Through this GCF Readiness project GCP/MCD/012/GCR, FAO supports the implementation of North Macedonia’s Enhanced NDC by strengthening institutional and technical capacities for integrated forest fire management and by improving national systems for collecting, analyzing, and sharing climate, greenhouse gas (GHG), and air-quality information. The forestry sector—traditionally the country’s main carbon sink—has become increasingly vulnerable to wildfires and land-use change, leading to rising GHG emissions and periodic deterioration of air quality with impacts on public health and ecosystems. 
The project strengthens integrated forest fire management through capacity development of key institutions, upgrading the Macedonian Forest Fire Information System (MKFFIS), and introducing technologies for near-real-time fire detection and monitoring in selected pilot areas. It develops forest vulnerability assessments, predictive fire-risk models, and national methodologies for fire prevention and mitigation, while supporting the preparation of a National Plan for Forest Fire Protection aligned with national climate mitigation goals. In parallel, the project enhances climate and environmental observation systems by strengthening the National Hydrometeorological Service’s capacities to monitor GHG emissions and air quality, particularly in forest-fire-prone areas. By improving climate observation, data transparency, and information sharing, the project enhances national preparedness, supports evidence-based mitigation action, reduces emissions linked to forest fires, improves understanding of fire-related air-pollution impacts, and contributes directly to North Macedonia’s decarbonization goals.
projects.outcome: Output 3.3: Environmental Protection and Natural Resource Management

It supports the strengthening of the institutional and technical capacities of the National Designated Authority (NDA) for the GCF and the institutions comprising the national GCF Country Coordination Mechanism to more effectively steer climate action and access to climate finance in North Macedonia. The project enhances the systems that enable these institutions to fulfil their roles and policy requirements by improving inter-institutional coordination, establishing knowledge management tools, and ensuring continuous capacity development. It also facilitates strategic private sector engagement in climate action, builds the capacities of direct access entities to meet and maintain GCF accreditation standards, and enables them to develop and implement high-quality GCF-funded projects. Furthermore, the project supports the updating of the national GCF Country Work Programme in line with national priorities and climate strategies, and contributes to the preparation of strong, nationally endorsed GCF concept notes and pre-feasibility assessments for priority climate investments.

Under this sub-output, FAO will support the Food and Veterinary Agency and MAFWE to control sheep pox and goat pox in North Macedonia, following the first confirmed outbreak in January 2026 and a sharp increase to over 90 confirmed outbreaks by September 2026. Emergency assistance will enable timely vaccine procurement while national procurement procedures are pursued, helping contain the outbreak and reduce the risk of further spread within the country and across borders.
Support will include vaccines and essential supplies for an emergency vaccination campaign targeting 200,000 sheep and goats, awareness raising, post-vaccination monitoring, strengthened passive surveillance and updated contingency, vaccination and surveillance plans. By protecting livestock assets, agricultural productivity and smallholder incomes, the intervention will help maintain an enabling environment for sustainable economic activity and decent work in the livestock sector, particularly for vulnerable rural households.
Practical training, simulation exercises and locally adapted technical learning materials will strengthen professional skills and institutional capacities for early detection, vaccination, biosecurity and effective outbreak response, supporting continuity of livestock production and greater resilience to future animal disease shocks.

projects.name: ITU Regional CyberDrill 2026
projects.description:
The ITU Cybersecurity Forum and CyberDrill for Europe and the Mediterranean will take place in Skopje, in October 2026. 

Combining a Cybersecurity Forum, technical trainings, and CyberDrill exercises, this event aims to enhance the communication and incident response capabilities of participating teams from European countries. It also seeks to foster collective and collaborative efforts to mitigate cyber threats among Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) from both Europe and the Arab regions of the Mediterranean.

This event continues ITU's tradition of organizing regional CyberDrills to build cybersecurity capacity and capability through collaboration and cooperation.

The primary objectives are to strengthen the cybersecurity readiness and resilience of the CSIRT community across Europe and the Mediterranean region. Specifically, to:
	•	Enhance cybersecurity capacity and capability through regional cooperation.
	•	Assist Member States in developing and implementing operational procedures to improve responses to various cyber incidents.
	•	Identify areas for improvement in future planning and CIRT processes at the national level.
	•	Strengthen international cooperation between Member States.
	•	Promote knowledge sharing to foster a regional culture of cybersecurity preparedness.

projects.description: Under this sub-output, FAO will support MAFWE and partner institutions to strengthen climate-responsive land management, agricultural investment readiness and policy development in North Macedonia. projects.name: FAO: Capacities of the National Hydrometeorological Service improved for air quality monitoring and data sharing through upgraded and integrated observation equipment
projects.description:
As part of the GCF Readiness project GCP/MCD/012/GCR, FAO supports the strengthening of national capacities of the National Hydrometeorological Service (NHMS) to enhance climate and air quality monitoring, expand and upgrade the observational network, and improve the use of climate and air quality data for mitigation in line with NDC commitments. This support includes an assessment of existing observational capacities and development of a technical proposal for an integrated network for sub-national and local GHG emissions estimation and air-quality monitoring, prioritizing co-location of monitoring systems and use of existing infrastructure.
In close cooperation with NHMS, the project will also support climate information-sharing mechanisms in at least three municipalities. Standardized reporting procedures and visual formats will translate locally relevant atmospheric and climate data into actionable recommendations for municipal authorities and stakeholders. Complemented by awareness-raising campaigns, these activities will strengthen capacities to interpret, communicate and use climate information for evidence-based mitigation decisions.

projects.name: FAO:  Enhancing Land Consolidation in North Macedonia
projects.description:
Under this sub-output, FAO, with support from the European Union, has assisted the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy to continue the implementation of the National Land Consolidation Programme. Key achievements include adoption of the National Land Consolidation Strategy and Action Plan 2025–2035, establishment of a Permanent Advisory Group on Land Consolidation, preparation and adoption of the land consolidation plan for Chiflik village, and completion of agricultural infrastructure works in Dabjani village. The project has also strengthened stakeholder capacities and public understanding of land consolidation.
Under the planned no-cost extension until 31 March 2027, remaining activities will include  targeted trainings for MAFWE, the National Extension Agency and the Agency for Real Estate Cadastre, focusing on multi-purpose land consolidation, cadastral registration and farmer engagement. A public awareness campaign will also be conducted to promote the National Land Consolidation Strategy and Action Plan 2025–2035 and opportunities for farmers to participate in future land consolidation projects. Infrastructure works originally planned for Chiflik and subsequently redirected to Logovardi will not be implemented.

projects.name: FAO: Veterinary and public health workforce capacities strengthened in animal disease surveillance, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), laboratory diagnostics and emergency preparedness through structured training and skills development programmes
projects.description: Under the Pandemic Fund-supported project "Strengthening One Health capacities for pandemic prevention, preparedness and response", FAO is implementing a set of interlinked workforce development and capacity building interventions targeting public institutions and civil society in the animal and public health sectors. FAO will review animal health training needs across the three KAM countries (North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo) and develop and deliver a Training of Trainers (ToT) programme for veterinary services, covering animal disease surveillance, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), biosecurity, and diagnostics. This will build sustainable institutional training capacity within national veterinary services. FAO will also establish a continuous professional development programme through accredited short courses for veterinary and public health professionals, with a focus on field epidemiology, outbreak investigation, foodborne disease surveillance, and data analysis. Additionally, structured laboratory training on the diagnosis of zoonotic diseases in livestock and wildlife, including AMR diagnostics (bacterial isolation, identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing), will be delivered to strengthen the qualified laboratory workforce. Joint outbreak simulation exercises will be conducted with WHO for public health and veterinary personnel to build cross-sector emergency preparedness and response competencies. FAO will also strengthen the capacities of community-based non-governmental organizations working with marginalized and vulnerable populations to improve One Health literacy and AMR awareness, contributing to inclusive skills development for civil society actors.

framework.name: Inclusive Social and Human Development
framework.description:
Strategic Priority 1: Inclusive Social and Human Development
The UN will work with partners to strengthen health, education, social protection, and GBV response systems to ensure equitable access and inclusion for all, especially vulnerable groups. Key focus areas include:

Health and Well-Being: Advancing primary health care, hospital reforms, universal health coverage, digital health systems, and healthy ageing, while addressing social determinants and health security under a One Health approach.
Inclusive, Quality Education: Expanding access to pre-school and quality education, optimizing school networks, promoting inclusive curricula, teacher training, and healthier learning environments, with targeted support for Roma, children with disabilities, and displaced children.
Responsive Social Protection: Enhancing policy frameworks, case management, and service delivery for vulnerable populations, introducing the European Child Guarantee, and improving coordination among social protection actors.
Gender-Based Violence Response: Strengthening institutional and multisectoral responses, survivor-centred services, and public awareness campaigns, aligned with the Istanbul Convention.

All interventions will uphold the principle of Leave No One Behind, engaging civil society, private sector, and government institutions to ensure inclusive, gender-responsive, and rights-based approaches.

Strategic Priority 2: Sustainable Economy and Decent Work
The UN will support North Macedonia in fostering an enabling economic environment, creating decent work opportunities, and promoting inclusive growth. Key focus areas include:

Economic Enabling Environment: Strengthening labour market institutions, addressing labour shortages, promoting labour mobility, integrating vulnerable groups, and supporting green transition and agri-food system resilience. Efforts also include enhancing trade and transport connectivity, cultural and creative industries, and innovation aligned with EU standards.
Vocational Training and Skills Development: Scaling up VET and lifelong learning, introducing green and digital curricula, and improving employability for women, youth, persons with disabilities, and rural populations. Special emphasis on care sector skills and part-time employment opportunities.
Women’s Economic Empowerment: Advancing gender equality in the labour market through policy reforms, research on pay gaps and unpaid care work, promoting family-friendly policies, and addressing barriers in STEM and ICT fields.

All interventions prioritize Leave No One Behind, ensuring vulnerable groups have equitable access to skills development and employment. Partnerships will include government institutions, private sector, social partners, civil society, and international development actors.

Strategic Priority 3: Resilient and Green Society and Ecosystems
The UN will support North Macedonia in advancing climate action, disaster resilience, pollution reduction, and biodiversity conservation to build a greener and more sustainable future. Key focus areas include:

Climate Action and Disaster Resilience: Developing gender-responsive climate policies, strengthening institutional capacities, accessing climate finance, and promoting clean energy solutions. Efforts include adaptation in agriculture, forestry, water, and health systems, and reforming disaster risk management in line with the Sendai Framework.
Pollution Action: Reducing air pollution from transport, industry, and waste burning; improving solid and hazardous waste management; promoting circular economy practices; and supporting compliance with Multilateral Environmental Agreements.
Environmental Protection and Natural Resource Management: Enhancing biodiversity conservation, managing protected areas and UNESCO sites, fostering transboundary cooperation, and integrating nature-based solutions into economic sectors. Focus also includes sustainable water and land management and citizen science initiatives.

All interventions prioritize Leave No One Behind, ensuring vulnerable groups are engaged and protected from climate and environmental risks. Partnerships will span government institutions, civil society, private sector, and international financing mechanisms to accelerate green transformation.

Strategic Priority 4: Rule of Law and Good Governance
The UN will support North Macedonia in strengthening governance, justice, and inclusive participation to advance EU accession and uphold human rights. Key focus areas include:

Good Governance: Enhancing institutional capacities, legislative alignment, decentralization reforms, and public service delivery. Support includes fiscal efficiency, gender-responsive budgeting, digital transformation, cybersecurity, and improved statistical systems for evidence-based policymaking.
Justice, Rule of Law, and Human Rights: Strengthening justice institutions, access to legal aid, anti-corruption measures, and compliance with international human rights standards. Efforts also address organized crime, trafficking, money laundering, and terrorism financing.
Women, Youth, and Civil Society Participation: Promoting inclusive decision-making and social cohesion through capacity building for women, youth, and civil society organizations, fostering accountability, and advancing gender-responsive governance.

All interventions prioritize Leave No One Behind, ensuring vulnerable groups’ rights and participation are integrated into governance and justice reforms. Partnerships will include government institutions, civil society, private sector, and international actors, including the EU and OSCE.
